item.title: PM announces National State of Disaster in response to ongoing El Nino
item.description: Cabinet has approved the declaration of a National State of Disaster covering the entire Republic of Fiji under section 91 of the National Disaster Risk Management Act, in response to the ongoing El Niño drought. Prime Minister, Sitiveni Rabuka says this is based on the advice of the National Disaster Risk Management Council.
item.content:encoded:
Cabinet has approved the declaration of a National State of Disaster covering the entire Republic of Fiji under section 91 of the National Disaster Risk Management Act, in response to the ongoing El Niño drought.

Prime Minister, Sitiveni Rabuka says this is based on the advice of the National Disaster Risk Management Council.

This means the government will now intensify it's response through coordinated action by all relevant ministries, departments, statutory authorities and divisional administrations under the established national disaster management arrangements.

The government has allocated $20 million for the national response through a redeployment of existing funds within ministries.

This funding will support emergency water supplies, assistance to affected communities, support for farmers and livestock owners, and other urgent interventions arising from the prolonged dry conditions.

Rabuka says the immediate priorities are to ensure affected communities have access to safe drinking water, strengthen emergency water carting and essential relief operations, maintain assessments to identify and respond to urgent needs, protect public health, sanitation and hygiene, support farmers, livestock owners and affected livelihoods and provide timely, accurate public information on conditions and the response.

He says particular attention will be given to remote and maritime communities, and to people who face additional difficulties accessing water and essential services.

Rabuka says this declaration strengthens the arrangements through which Government mobilises resources, coordinates assistance and supports communities facing increasing hardship.

He says it builds on the response already underway and provides for its escalation as needs increase.

Under section 93, the declaration will remain in force for the period specified in it, which must not exceed 30 days.

Cabinet may extend or revoke the declaration on the advice of the National Disaster Risk Management Council.

Rabuka says he knows that families across Fiji are concerned about the availability of water and the effects of prolonged dry conditions on their daily lives.

He says farmers are worried about their crops and livestock, while communities, particularly in remote and maritime areas, face growing pressure on their water supplies.

The Prime Minister says these concerns are real and their decisions must continue to be grounded in verified conditions, technical advice and the needs of our people.

Rabuka says over the past month, Government has delivered more than two million litres of emergency water to affected maritime communities.

The Water Authority of Fiji has also been supplying emergency water to affected communities on the mainland.

He adds the Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Sugar Industry has rolled out six initiatives to assist farmers.

These cover emergency water and irrigation; livestock feed; climate resilient planting materials and seed; sugar sector drought protection; household and community food security; and sustainable agricultural practices.

The Prime Minister says the Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection has increased the monthly eTransport top-up under the Transport Assistance Scheme to assist eligible beneficiaries with rising transport costs during the ongoing El Niño impacts.

The increase applies to older persons holding purple eTransport cards and persons with disabilities holding green eTransport cards.

The Prime Minister says they will also continue working with development partners, humanitarian organisations, the private sector, faith-based organisations and community representatives.

item.title: Grammar Dux Darlene Papamau dedicates top award to her parents
item.description: For 18-year-old Darlene Papamau, being named the Dux of Suva Grammar School is more than just an academic achievement, it is a moment dedicated to the sacrifices and support of her parents. The emotional moment brought tears to Darlene’s eyes as she received the top award during the school’s graduation ceremony today.
item.content:encoded:
For 18-year-old Darlene Papamau, being named the Dux of Suva Grammar School is more than just an academic achievement, it is a moment dedicated to the sacrifices and support of her parents.

The emotional moment brought tears to Darlene’s eyes as she received the top award during the school’s graduation ceremony today.

Originally from Tuvalu, Darlene says her achievement means everything to her, especially knowing how much her parents have done to support her and her siblings throughout their education.

As the eldest daughter in the family, she recognises the sacrifices her parents have made, including paying extra expenses to ensure she could reach this milestone.

For Darlene, the award is a way of honouring their hard work, love and commitment to her education.

Despite being recognised as the school’s top student, Darlene never expected her name to be called for the Dux award.

The announcement came as a complete surprise, making the moment even more emotional for her.

Looking ahead, Darlene hopes to secure a scholarship to Australia, where she plans to pursue her dream of studying aerospace engineering.

She also acknowledged the role of her faith, thanking God for His blessings, her friends for their encouragement throughout the year, and her parents for their continued love and sacrifices.

Darlene also has an encouraging message for students who may doubt their abilities, reminding them not to give up on themselves.

She admits she once doubted whether she was good enough to receive such an award, but believes that with faith and determination, anything is possible.

item.title: 12-year-old boy injured while rescuing his two younger siblings from Tacirua house fire
item.description: A 12-year-old boy has suffered burns while rescuing his two younger siblings who were trapped inside a house during a fire on Princes Road, Tacirua, this morning. NFA says the boy sustained burns to both hands, his stomach, back and down to his knees.
item.content:encoded:
A 12-year-old boy has suffered burns while rescuing his two younger siblings who were trapped inside a house during a fire on Princes Road, Tacirua, this morning.

NFA says the boy sustained burns to both hands, his stomach, back and down to his knees.

He was taken to a health centre for medical attention.

NFA says firefighters were informed that neighbours and occupants had already extinguished the fire using buckets of water and a garden hose.

They say preliminary information indicates that the fire may have started after children were playing with matches inside the home.

NFA Chief Executive Officer Puamau Sowane says children playing with matches is extremely dangerous and can have devastating consequences, urging parents and guardians to keep matches and lighters securely out of children's reach.

Sowane says while the 12-year-old's actions demonstrate extraordinary courage, no child should ever be placed in a situation where they have to risk their life because of a preventable fire.

The NFA is also reminding members of the public to evacuate immediately if a fire breaks out, ensure everyone is accounted for and call 910 for assistance.

item.content:encoded:
The case against former sports coach, Guy Morris, who is accused of sexually assaulting three girls in Suva, has been adjourned to December 8th for mention.

Morris appeared before Magistrate Jospeh Daurewa this morning . Morris is facing eight counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault. It is alleged that he sexually assaulted three girls, aged 13, 14 and 16 years, between February 2023 to March 2024. The matter is adjourned for mention, with the Pre-Trial Conference (PTC) date to be determined.
